title: Long-Horizon Monitoring Degradation: Do Monitors Lose Effectiveness as Task Length Increases?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If monitoring degrades with task length, current short-task evaluations overestimate safety. This finding directly affects how we interpret monitoring results and design long-horizon deployments. Clear practical implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing or adapting tasks of three length tiers requires significant effort. METR tasks may not naturally scale to 150 steps. Context summarization implementation adds complexity. API-only but task construction is the bottleneck.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three task length tiers, each with multiple tasks, plus a summarization mitigation experiment. Task construction/adaptation is the most time-consuming part and could easily exceed 30 hours. Needs to be narrowed to 2 tiers.
